title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Midterm Swell: Dow Rides a 1,500-Point Wave
conditions.summary: Stocks rallied broadly the day after Democrats won both chambers of Congress, with the Dow up 3% and the S&P 500 up 1.6%. Oil plunged about 8% while energy and chip stocks lagged.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: Dow closed at 53,356.12, up 1,569 points or 3.03%.
S&P 500 closed at 7,688.62, up 1.58%; Nasdaq Composite closed at 25,736.51, up 1.44%; Russell 2000 closed at 2,856.96, up 1.58%.
Democrats won control of the House and Senate; futures fell overnight, then rebounded after President Trump said he would accept the results, with investors betting on gridlock.
S&P 500 peaked near +1.9% in early afternoon before fading into the close; only 4 of 30 Dow stocks were down late in the day.
Best sectors: consumer discretionary (+4.3%), financials (+3.5%), communication services (+3.5%), health care (+3.1%). Worst: energy (-4.7%), industrials (-1.1%), semiconductors (-2.8%).

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: ISM services PMI for October was 54.5, just below the 54.8 forecast; the prices index eased to 73.0.
ADP private payrolls rose 86,000 in October, above the roughly 69,000 expected.
WTI crude fell about 8% to near $88 on hopes the new Congress pushes to wind down the Iran war; Brent fell below $100.
The 10-year Treasury yield eased to about 4.89%, down 5 to 9 basis points depending on the source; gold rose back above $4,000 and bitcoin back above $80,000.
Fed funds futures still show close to 80% odds of a rate hike at the December 9 Fed meeting.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: MSFT (Microsoft): +6.7% — megacap tech led the rally.
AAPL (Apple): +5.3% — treated as a safe haven within tech after its quarterly report.
NXT (Nextracker): +11.1% — solar stocks jumped on the Democratic sweep.
SHOP (Shopify): +7.3% — rode a strong consumer discretionary rally.
NVDA (Nvidia): -3.2% — chip stocks fell on fears of tighter AI and data-center rules.
DDOG (Datadog): -14.4% — slid despite topping earnings estimates.
CVS (CVS Health): -12.5% — fell after announcing plans to split into two companies by 2028, despite beating estimates.
ETN (Eaton): -9.9% — dropped with data-center suppliers after Texas's governor-elect pledged a pause on new data centers.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: Before the open: McDonald's beat on profit but missed on revenue, and was up more than 5% in the afternoon.
Before the open: Uber beat but guided Q4 profit below estimates; shares were still up about 7% in the afternoon.
After the close: AppLovin beat on revenue and profit with strong Q4 guidance; shares jumped about 18% to 21% after hours.
After the close: Qualcomm beat on revenue but its outlook disappointed; shares fell about 7% after hours.
After the close: Zillow missed estimates and guided low (down about 16%); Snap fell about 9% and HubSpot about 4% on soft outlooks; Coherent rose about 5% after a beat and raise.

sections.title: Business News
items: Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has pledged a pause on new data centers, weighing on AI infrastructure stocks.
Riot Platforms leased its Corsicana, Texas campus to an AI lab in a deal worth about $28 billion over 15 years.
Qualcomm reportedly agreed to supply network technology for SpaceX's US mobile service.
CVS Health plans to separate into two public companies by the first half of 2028.
Treasury's quarterly refunding statement dropped the words "at least" from its pledge on steady auction sizes, opening the door to changes next year.

sections.title: On Deck
items: 7:30 AM CT: weekly jobless claims and preliminary Q3 productivity.
Fed speakers: Cleveland Fed's Beth Hammack and Richmond Fed's Tom Barkin (times not yet confirmed).
Before the open: ConocoPhillips, Cigna, Duke Energy, Cummins, Air Products.
After the close: Airbnb, Cloudflare, Monster Beverage, Atlassian, Microchip Technology.
Friday: October jobs report at 7:30 AM CT.

Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Wednesday, November fourth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Sunset Session, the full wrap of today's market. The sun is sliding down over the water on the last set of the day. Gus the wonder dog sat on the deck all day watching the election swell roll in. Say good evening, Gus! [BARK]

Let's talk about the final set. The day after the midterms, with Democrats taking both the House and the Senate, stocks paddled out hard. The Dow surged three percent, more than fifteen hundred points, to fifty three thousand three hundred fifty six. The S and P five hundred rose one point six percent to seven thousand six hundred eighty nine. The Nasdaq gained one point four percent, and the Russell two thousand climbed one point six percent. Futures wiped out overnight, then the swell flipped once the President said he would accept the results and work with the new Congress. Consumer, financial, communication and health care stocks led. Energy was the big wipeout, and chip stocks slipped.

Now the wind and weather. Crude oil crashed about eight percent to around eighty eight dollars, on hopes a new Congress pushes harder to wind down the Iran war. The ten year Treasury yield eased to about four point eight nine percent. Gold jumped more than three percent, back above four thousand dollars, and bitcoin climbed back above eighty thousand. The fear gauge, the VIX, dropped sharply. On the data, the ISM services index came in at fifty four point five, a touch under forecasts. The A D P report showed eighty six thousand private jobs, better than expected. Traders still see good odds of a Fed rate hike in December.

Time to check the lineup. Microsoft was the Kahuna today, up nearly seven percent. Gus, that's worth a biscuit! Here you go, buddy! [SNACK] Apple rose more than five percent, and solar names like Nextracker were stoked, up eleven percent. On the gnarly side, Nvidia fell about three percent and data center plays took a beating after Texas's governor elect pledged a pause on new data centers. Datadog sank fourteen percent, and C V S Health dropped twelve and a half percent after laying out a plan to split in two.

On the tide chart, McDonald's beat on profit but missed on sales, and still rallied. Uber beat but gave a soft outlook. After the bell, AppLovin hung ten, jumping about twenty percent on a big beat and strong guidance. Qualcomm slid about seven percent on its outlook, and Zillow dropped about sixteen percent after missing estimates.

In beach talk, Riot Platforms leased its Texas campus to an A I lab in a deal worth about twenty eight billion dollars. Qualcomm signed on to provide network tech for SpaceX mobile service.

Here's tomorrow's forecast. Jobless claims and productivity land at seven thirty A M Central. Fed speakers Beth Hammack and Tom Barkin are on the schedule. ConocoPhillips and Cigna report in the morning, and Airbnb and Cloudflare after the close. Friday brings the big jobs report.
